title: Sprint 9 - Set Operations & Advanced Schema
description: Complete all SQL queries in this sprint.

tickets.title: Find Alice's Tasks via Subquery
tickets.description: Find all task titles for the user 'alice_dev' without using a JOIN, but instead using a subquery.
tasks: Find all task titles for the user 'alice_dev' without using a JOIN, but instead using a subquery.
learning_objectives: Writing Subqueries in the WHERE clause.
common_mistakes: Using = when subquery returns multiple rows (use IN instead in that case).
hints: Read the MySQL documentation for the specific keyword.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT title FROM todos WHERE user_id = (SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = 'alice_dev') ORDER BY title;

tickets.title: User Task Counts (CTE)
tickets.description: Use a Common Table Expression (CTE) named `user_counts` to calculate the total tasks per user_id, then select all records from the CTE.
tasks: Use a Common Table Expression (CTE) named `user_counts` to calculate the total tasks per user_id, then select all records from the CTE.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to SELECT from the CTE after defining it.
hints: Read the MySQL documentation for the specific keyword.

scoring_rules.system_query: WITH user_counts AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) as total_tasks FROM todos GROUP BY user_id) SELECT * FROM user_counts ORDER BY user_id;

tickets.description: The product team wants to track when a task was last updated. Add a new column `updated_at` of type DATE to the `todos` table.
tasks: The product team wants to track when a task was last updated. Add a new column `updated_at` of type DATE to the `todos` table.
